preconditions.description: The input is a single integer n representing the board size, where 3 ≤ n ≤ 100.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.split()) == n and all(len(line) == n for line in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly n lines, each containing exactly n characters ('W' or 'B').

postconditions.expression: all(cell in ('W', 'B') for line in stdout.split() for cell in line)
postconditions.description: Each cell in the output grid is assigned either 'W' (white knight) or 'B' (black knight).

postconditions.expression: let grid = [list(line) for line in stdout.split()]; let duels = sum(1 for (i1, j1), (i2, j2) in [(i1, j1, i2, j2) for i1 in range(n) for j1 in range(n) for i2 in range(n) for j2 in range(n) if (abs(i1 - i2) == 2 and abs(j1 - j2) == 1) or (abs(i1 - i2) == 1 and abs(j1 - j2) == 2) and grid[i1][j1] != grid[i2][j2]]; let max_possible_duels = sum(1 for i1 in range(n) for j1 in range(n) for i2 in range(n) for j2 in range(n) if (abs(i1 - i2) == 2 and abs(j1 - j2) == 1) or (abs(i1 - i2) == 1 and abs(j1 - j2) == 2)); duels == max_possible_duels
postconditions.description: The output grid maximizes the number of duels (pairs of knights of different colors that attack each other). A duel exists between two knights at (i1, j1) and (i2, j2) if they are of different colors and satisfy the knight's attack condition (|x1 - x2| = 2 and |y1 - y2| = 1, or |x1 - x2| = 1 and |y1 - y2| = 2).
